rights_boundary.mechanical_inspiration: Classic arcade maze chase: maze routing, required collectibles, distinct pursuers, temporary reversal pickups, bonus route temptations, escalating pressure.
do_not_copy: sprites, colors, sounds, fruit identities, or trade dress
specific ghost names or exact personality implementation details
rights_boundary.safe_direction: Use an original grid, original entities, original theme, and generalized pursuit/reversal rules.

theme_pitch.player_role: A small maintenance drone sent through a cathedral-sized machine to reclaim live rivets before the choir-security system seals the nave.
theme_pitch.floor_goal: reclaim every charged rivet or unlock a rare emergency exit module

core_loop: Enter a generated compact maze floor.
Read the four active pursuer rules and one floor modifier.
Route through charged rivets while avoiding normal-contact death.
Use breaker overloads to reverse predator/prey pressure briefly.
Decide whether bonus salvage is worth a route detour.
Clear required rivets, choose one upgrade, advance to a harder floor.

movement_model_options.summary: Continuous tile-grid movement with buffered turns at intersections.
movement_model_options.best_for: faithful arcade tension and mobile joystick/swipe feel
movement_model_options.risk: harder to make procedural floors feel fair

movement_model_options.summary: Player and pursuers move on fixed ticks; input queues before intersections.
Player moves one tile per turn; pursuers move by speed budgets and mode rules.
movement_model_options.risk: can stop feeling like maze chase

required_properties: at least two loops around the central zone
pursuer home/spawn zone visible near center
no required dead-end rivets unless marked as greed clusters
maze_generation.generation_strategy: Assemble hand-authored chunks into a symmetric-ish maze, then run reachability and loop checks. Avoid fully random carving for the first prototype.

pursuers.base_rule: Targets the player position through shortest route.
Targets a tile several steps ahead of player movement direction.
Targets intersections near the player's likely escape route.
Alternates chase and scatter on a visible timer, with deterministic tie-breaking.
mutation_examples: leaves a delayed echo every few turns

floor_modifiers.label: Alarm Rivets
floor_modifiers.effect: Greed clusters raise pursuer speed for a short window after collection.

floor_modifiers.label: Flicker-Lit Nave
floor_modifiers.effect: Pursuer target markers are visible only near intersections.

floor_modifiers.label: One-Way Current
floor_modifiers.effect: Some corridors force direction until the next intersection.

floor_modifiers.label: Overloaded Breakers
floor_modifiers.effect: Reversal lasts less time, but eating a pursuer opens one gate.

floor_modifiers.label: Salvage Liturgy
floor_modifiers.effect: Bonus reliquary appears more often, but one pursuer shadows its route.

player_upgrades.label: Early Turn Buffer
player_upgrades.route_effect: Queue one turn earlier at intersections.

player_upgrades.label: Static Decoy
player_upgrades.route_effect: Drop a lure that redirects one pursuer at a junction.

player_upgrades.label: Breaker Bite
player_upgrades.route_effect: Reversal is shorter, but eating a pursuer grants a speed burst.

player_upgrades.label: Greed Magnet
player_upgrades.route_effect: Pull nearby rivets into the player, but alert pursuers.

player_upgrades.label: Gate Key
player_upgrades.route_effect: Open one locked gate per floor.

player_upgrades.label: Echo Step
player_upgrades.route_effect: First lethal contact per floor rewinds three tiles, then burns out.

scoring_rules.greed_clusters: optional higher score and upgrade currency
scoring_rules.reversal_chain: higher rewards for eating multiple pursuers in one overload
scoring_rules.routing_chain_bonus: reward long collection chains without reversing direction

validation_checks: maze has at least two loops
reversal pickups reachable before unavoidable contact
pursuer target rules deterministic for a seed
no required collectible appears in an unmarked lethal dead-end
bonus reliquary can be reached and ignored by different viable routes
each upgrade changes at least one route decision
open_questions: Should the first prototype be Godot or browser canvas?
Should generated floors use chunk assembly or hand-authored floor templates first?
Should upgrades persist across runs or stay run-local?
Should the theme skew grim industrial, comic arcade, or sacred machine horror?
